title: 1. Archive-first: does long recovery ramp-out suppress Stage-B rolling?
hypothesis: In the weak replication lineage (lineage 2 of R-128), rolling among re-captured episodes improves around the end of recovery support by more than in the other four lineages. The inference is limited to this lineage's release-associated rolling pattern: no causal attribution and no claim about the recipe's reliability.

prediction.against: R-128: equal-weight mean of the other four Stage-B lineages
prediction.rationale: Measure the change in rolling-step fraction from the 30 steps before support ends to the 30 steps afterward; lineage 2 should show at least 0.10 more release-associated improvement. This tests the Stage-B variance mechanism suggested by D-088, not D-090's healthy-hand-back failures. All proposals cost zero episodes; Q1 priority breaks the information-per-episode tie.

protocol.command: gpu run 'source ~/IsaacLab/source_env.sh && timeout 900s python -u scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py --study stage_b_release_audit'
code_changes: lares/envs/isaac_pen_spin/stage_b_release_audit.py (new, archive only; registered in scripts/run_shadowhand_spin_stages.py with a block in config/shadowhand_spin_stages.yaml), reusing recovery_handback_audit's trigger reconstruction. Reads only R-128's archived Stage-B cells logs/pen_spin/r128_training_replication/confirmation/s<seed>/L<k>_B_cell.{json,npz} (five lineages x 24 shared manifests) and each lineage's frozen stage-B parameters; no simulator episode, no model call, no new seed or manifest.

Frozen before any outcome is computed: each lineage's decision step and support end come from its own stage-B parameters; a case is eligible if its reconstructed trigger fired and it is still in play 30 steps after its support end; the statistic per case is the rolling-step fraction (the success predicate) in the 30 steps after support ends minus the 30 steps before. No case is excluded on its post-release rolling. Report eligible counts per lineage.

Registered quantity (gate_statistics): lineage 2's mean post-minus-pre change minus the equal-weight mean of the other four lineages' mean changes, with a case-level 95% interval (cases of the 24 shared manifests) and a manifest-clustered interval beside it. Supported with the lower bound >= 0.10; refuted with the upper bound < 0.10; otherwise inconclusive; an interval spanning zero establishes no directional difference.
Ceiling: 0 simulator episodes, 0 LLM calls, 15 minutes. If required archive data are missing the audit is inconclusive; no replacement rollout.

falsified_by: The upper 95% interval bound on lineage 2's excess release-associated improvement is below 0.10; an interval spanning the threshold is inconclusive, and one spanning zero establishes no directional difference.

result.notes: Archive only (R-128's stage-B cells, five lineages x 24 shared manifests, 3,072 cases each); no episode, no model call; definitions committed (867bf43) before the audit ran. Among reconstructed-triggered cases still in play 30 steps after support ends (863-995 per lineage), the rolling-step fraction rises by 0.166 / 0.321 / 0.186 / 0.092 / 0.313 across the end of support in lineages 0-4. Lineage 2's change minus the mean of the other four is -0.037, 95% interval [-0.064, -0.011] (manifest-clustered [-0.057, -0.014]): the upper bound is far below +0.10, so the hypothesis is REFUTED; lineage 2 shows, if anything, slightly less release-associated improvement. The premise was also off at this stage: all five stage-B modules have long ramp-outs (22-42 steps) and stroke multipliers near 1 (1.01-1.23), so lineage 2 (42.4, 1.02) is not distinctive after 12 updates; its long ramp-out only stands out at the later stages. Triggers are reconstructed, one lineage is one lineage, and the comparison is an association around the end of support.

verdicts.reasoning: By the frozen rule: lineage 2's post-minus-pre rolling change around the end of support minus the other four lineages' mean is -0.037 [-0.064, -0.011]; the upper bound is below +0.10 (and below zero). The stage-B modules of all five lineages look alike (ramp-out 22-42 steps, stroke multiplier near 1), so the weak lineage's stage-B deficit is not a support-release effect.
verdicts.next_experiment: Do not pursue support-release explanations of the Q1 variance. Run the already approved R-135 archive audit, then let the loop's exhaustion rule return the decision to the user.

verdicts.reasoning: Against the registered equal-weight mean of the other four Stage-B lineages, lineage 2's gate_statistics contrast was -0.03745, with a 95% interval of [-0.06429, -0.01061] [logs/pen_spin/r134_stage_b_release/summary.json]. Its upper bound is below the predicted increase of +0.10, satisfying the registered falsification rule [logs/pen_spin/r134_stage_b_release/summary.json]. The manifest-clustered sensitivity agrees: mean -0.03568, interval [-0.05741, -0.01395], also entirely negative [logs/pen_spin/r134_stage_b_release/summary.json]. This supports less release-associated improvement in the weak lineage relative to the named control, but the survivor-conditioned, release-aligned comparison establishes neither causal support suppression nor recipe reliability [logs/pen_spin/r134_stage_b_release/summary.json].
